title: Per-caller priority shares and deferred-billing principles for soft-degradation
creator: Priya Nambiar
description: Problem statement: Some customers run mixed-criticality workloads where a small subset of callers must maintain low latency while others can be opportunistically deferred. Current plan entitlements and quotas are strict buckets (per-plan tokens, per-route quotas) and do not support per-caller prioritization or deferred billing semantics. This PRD defines product requirements and acceptance criteria for a feature that exposes per-caller priority shares, a deferred-billing mode (defer invoicing for best-effort usage windows), and predictable soft-degradation rules so customers can opt-in to lower-cost degraded behavior under congestion.
goals: Allow customers to assign priority shares to API keys or callers so that traffic is proportionally prioritized when contention occurs
Introduce a deferred-billing window for best-effort usage that shifts billing events to a later reconciliation step rather than immediate overage charges
Define deterministic soft-degradation rules (per-route and per-tenant) so degraded responses and fallbacks are predictable and observable
Provide clear acceptance criteria and telemetry to validate correctness and customer impact
background: Enterprise customers have requested predictable cost controls and graceful degradation for bursty ML workloads (e.g., search re-rank vs. user-facing chat). Sales and Solutions report repeated asks for: per-key prioritization, temporary deferred billing for non-critical batch jobs, and deterministic fallbacks to cheaper model variants when saturation occurs. This reduces operational alerts and invoice surprises.
out_of_scope: Changing global plan pricing or rate card
Implementing new hardware-level QoS (this is runtime/policy configuration only)
in_scope: API surface to attach a priority_share integer to an API key or caller identity
Control-plane UI in Console to create deferred-billing windows and assign policies
Runtime policy enforcement for proportional request admission and deterministic fallback ordering
Billing pipeline flag to mark usage as deferred and reconciliation rules for the deferred window
requirements: R1: Allow per-caller integer priority_share (1-1000) attached to API key with default 100
R2: Admission controller must use weighted fair share across simultaneous callers to enforce proportional throughput when under contention
R3: Admins can create named deferred_billing_windows (start,end,eligible_routes) via Console or API
R4: Deferred usage must be tagged in metering as deferred:true and excluded from real-time overage triggers
R5: Deferred usage is subject to a reconciliation policy: either auto-bill at window close or require manual approval
R6: Soft-degradation fallbacks should follow a predictable ordered list: primary model -> cheaper quantized variant -> cached prefix response -> 503 with retry-after header
R7: Console UI shows per-caller priority share metrics, deferred usage totals, and projected invoice delta before reconciliation
R8: Admins can set per-plan maximum deferred capacity (percentage of committed capacity or absolute tokens)
R9: Audit logs for priority and deferred policy changes must be sent to the enterprise audit stream (KMS/HSM integration not required here)
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Weighted admission must add no more than 2ms median p99 overhead to request path under no-contention
NFR2: Tagging for deferred usage must not increase billing delay beyond existing metering SLA of 5 minutes
NFR3: Telemetry must be queryable in Console within 30s of event emission
NFR4: System must default to safe behavior (deny deferred billing reconciliation if reconciliation fails)
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Given three callers with priority_shares 200,100,100 and total throughput limit of 200 qps, measured served QPS in steady-state should be within ±5% proportional ratio 100:50:50
AC2: When deferred_billing_window is active for a caller, billing records for eligible routes are marked deferred:true and do not trigger overage billing until reconciliation
AC3: Reconciliation modes (auto-bill/manual) behave as configured: auto-bill charges invoices at window close; manual requires explicit approval and audit trail
AC4: Under saturation, soft-degradation follows the ordered fallback for 99% of requests; deviations must be logged and reviewed
AC5: Console displays projected invoice delta from deferred usage with a disclaimer and a confidence band, accuracy within 10% of final reconciliation for test synthetic workloads
AC6: Metrics and traces show the admission controller decisions with caller_id, priority_share, decision (serve/defer/fallback), and timestamp for at least 30 days
AC7: Security review completed and any PII handling documented before release
rollout_plan: Phase 0: API and control-plane feature gated behind 'priority-shares' feature flag; internal dogfood for Redwood services only
Phase 1: Limited beta with 3 customers; enable deferred windows and weighted admission; collect telemetry and billing reconciliation artifacts
Phase 2: feedback iteration, fix any reconciliation edge cases, scale test to multi-tenant load
Phase 3: Gradual public release with opt-in billing reconciliation and Console defaults set to safe manual mode
notes: Design trade-off: priority_shares are integer-weighted instead of explicit QPS caps to keep control-plane simpler and support proportional fairness
Edge-case: callers with priority_share 0 will be denied unless a special emergency override is applied
Billing teams requested a conservative auto-bill default to avoid surprise refunds; default will be manual approval for GA
